nodes.text:
From the car park you count them: ground, one, two, three, four. Four rows of glass on a building that insists it has three floors, and the top row has curtains in it.

Somebody was very careful about the inside of this building and forgot the outside entirely.

The stairwell ends at three. You have walked it twice to be certain, once counting.

The lift panel has buttons for G to 3 and then a smooth grey gap where 4 would go, and you are standing on the fourth floor reading it.

choices.text: Count the windows from the car park

nodes.text:
The sticker gives a firm, a phone number, a date — and a line of block capitals naming the equipment it covers.

**GOODS LIFT — 4TH FLR LANDING.** Serviced every spring, for years, for a landing that is not on any plan in the building.

You let the doors close and ride down to three, where the building agrees with itself and nothing needs explaining.

It is an enormous relief for about four minutes.

The doors open onto nothing — shaft wall, brick, a smell of old grease.

At knee height there is a maintenance sticker, laminated, with a date from last spring. Somebody has been servicing something up here. Recently. On a schedule.

The flat brass key from the fire panel fits, because of course it does — every fire panel in every building of this age takes the same key, and that is the whole reason it is there.

Behind the steel doors: a platform, a folding grille, and a lever worn smooth by a very great many hands.

The cupboard on four is unlocked and almost empty: a wall of pipework, a dead fluorescent tube, and bolted beside them a pair of steel doors far too wide to belong in a cupboard.

No call button. One keyhole, brass, worn bright.

choices.text: Find something that fits the keyhole

game.objective: Find the way out of a floor that officially does not exist.
game.briefing: Everything in this building agrees that you are not here. Find the one thing that does not.
game.solution_key: the service lift | service lift | goods lift | the goods lift | goods hoist
game.answer_hint: It is a piece of machinery, and the building has been paying to maintain it.

story.title: The Building Does Not Have a Fourth Floor
story.description: The stairwell ends at three. The lifts stop at three. You are standing on four.
story.author: Priya Nain
